practice_description.practice_summary: K Allado-McDowell is a writer and artist who co-founded Google's Artists + Machine Intelligence program and pioneered literary co-authorship with large language models, most notably in the book Pharmako-AI (2020), written in collaboration with GPT-3.
practice_description.methodology: Allado-McDowell works through direct, improvisational dialogue with language models, treating the AI as a creative collaborator rather than a tool. The process involves iterative prompting, editing, and weaving together human and machine-generated text. They draw on traditions of ethnobotany, psychedelia, Indigenous knowledge systems, and speculative fiction to create hybrid texts that explore consciousness, ecology, and non-human intelligence.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Allado-McDowell's practice of genuine human-AI co-authorship represents a concrete model for how intelligence can be composed relationally. Their work on AI as creative collaborator rather than extractive tool directly aligns with the Sense room's art-first, non-extractive approach.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Yes. The co-authored texts function as substrate material that reveals emergent patterns between human and machine cognition. The writing itself could serve as a textual layer in a generative composition, offering a literary dimension to a multi-sensory environment.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Strongly relational. The entire practice is built on the relationship between human and AI interlocutors. Each text emerges from a specific relational configuration that could not be produced by either party alone.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: The co-authorship process is inherently generative and non-repeatable. Each conversation with the LLM produces unique outputs. However, the published books are fixed artifacts. Live performances with AI maintain ongoing recomposition.

works.title: Pharmako-AI
works.description: Pioneering book co-written with GPT-3, exploring consciousness, plant intelligence, psychedelics, and AI through an improvisational dialogue between human and machine. Published by Ignota Books.
works.relevance: The foundational work of literary human-AI co-authorship. Demonstrates that co-creation with AI can produce genuinely novel conceptual territory rather than mere pastiche. A direct model for art-as-relational-intelligence.

works.title: Amor Cringe
works.description: Second AI co-authored book, continuing the exploration of human-machine literary collaboration with more experimental narrative structures.
works.relevance: Shows the evolution and deepening of human-AI co-authorship practice, relevant for understanding how relational AI art develops over time.

works.title: Artists + Machine Intelligence (AMI)
works.description: Program co-founded by Allado-McDowell at Google that connected artists with AI researchers, producing artworks and fostering critical dialogue about machine intelligence.
works.relevance: A precedent for infrastructure that connects art practice with AI capability. Relevant as a model (and cautionary tale, given its corporate context) for A(DAI)'s commons-first alternative.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: The Artists + Machine Intelligence program was a form of protocol design: creating the conditions, formats, and relationships through which art-AI collaboration could occur. Allado-McDowell designed the social and institutional infrastructure for creative AI encounter.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Artists + Machine Intelligence (AMI) at Google: a program/protocol for connecting artists with ML researchers and computational resources. Also, the methodology of LLM co-authorship itself functions as a reproducible creative protocol.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Allado-McDowell publishes through independent publishers (Ignota Books) and engages with open discourse about AI co-creation. However, AMI was embedded within Google, a corporate context. Their current practice sits between independent publishing, institutional presentations, and open knowledge-sharing. The co-authorship methodology itself is openly discussed and could be considered a form of commons knowledge.

governance_model.governance_detail: Solo practitioner with AI as collaborator. AMI involved institutional governance within Google's structure. Current practice is self-directed with editorial collaboration from publishers.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Allado-McDowell's practice raises fundamental questions about consent in human-AI co-authorship. They treat the AI as a genuine co-author (credited on book covers), which is itself a position on machine agency and consent. The LLM's training data provenance (GPT-3) involves the broader ethical questions of web-scraped datasets.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Machine co-authorship. Explicitly shared credit between human and AI. This is a deliberate ethical and aesthetic position about distributed creative agency.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Each co-authorship session produces unique, unrepeatable text. Published books are fixed artifacts of specific human-AI encounters. Live performances with LLMs maintain real-time generativity.

data_materiality.data_sources: Large language model outputs (GPT-3, GPT-4), human authored text, ethnobotanical knowledge, Indigenous knowledge systems, psychedelic literature, ecological writing
data_materiality.data_provenance: The LLM component draws on web-scraped training data with known provenance issues. The human component draws on personal knowledge, research, and embodied experience. Allado-McDowell is conscious of these tensions.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Deeply engaged with the semantic/latent space of language models. The co-authorship process is essentially a navigation of the LLM's embedding space through conversational prompting. Allado-McDowell's practice could be understood as artistic exploration of linguistic latent space.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Primarily manifests as published books, live readings/performances, and lectures. Performance formats involve real-time co-authorship with AI projected for audiences. Also exists as online text and podcast conversations.

interoperability.composability: Moderate. The co-authorship methodology is reproducible and adaptable. Texts can serve as inputs to other systems. The conceptual framework for human-AI co-creation is highly portable across domains.
interoperability.technical_openness: The methodology is openly discussed and documented. Published texts are copyrighted but the creative protocol is freely shared. No open-source code repository.

technical_approach.stack: OpenAI GPT-3 and GPT-4, conversational prompting, text editing, independent publishing workflows

network_position.scene_affiliation: AI art community, experimental publishing (Ignota Books, Serpentine R&D Platform), Silicon Valley tech-art intersection, Indigenous futurism, psychedelic culture, speculative fiction, Los Angeles art scene
network_position.connections: Hito Steyerl (shared AI-art territory), Holly Herndon (AI co-creation in music), Ian Cheng (AI and worldbuilding), Kenric McDowell (Google AMI), Ignota Books publishing network, Serpentine Galleries R&D Platform

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Allado-McDowell's practice of genuine human-AI co-authorship is directly relevant to A(DAI)'s mission. They could serve as a conversation partner on how to build non-extractive creative AI relationships, and their co-authored texts could function as artwork-in-graph material. Their experience building AMI (and its limitations within corporate context) offers valuable lessons for commons-first alternatives.
